About the Personal Care event

Personal Care is a Health Professions event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: skills · online submission. This event has special eligibility requirements, so check the guidelines with your advisor.

Ten step-by-step lessons for the HOSA Personal Care event (for members classified under IDEA), following the 2026–27 guidelines and all eight rating sheets: handwashing, PPE, unoccupied and occupied beds, admitting, transfer, vital signs (TPR and aneroid blood pressure) and ostomy care. Each lesson uses plain language, numbered steps that match the rating sheet, ordering drills, flip cards and practice scenarios. Remember to upload the IEP Verification and Accommodation Form by May 15. Always follow the scenario the judge reads to you.

Personal Care lessons

Unit 1 · The event, the caregiver role and infection control

Eligibility, how the skills round works and Skills I and II.

  1. The Personal Care event and the caregiver role 35 min

    Personal Care lets you show what a caregiver does: keep people clean, safe, comfortable and respected. There is no written test. Instead you perform real skills while judges watch. This lesson explains how the event…

  2. Handwashing (Skill I) 30 min

    Germs are too small to see, but they travel on hands from one person to another. Washing your hands the right way is the best way to stop them. Skill I has 21 steps, and you have 3 minutes.

  3. Putting on and taking off PPE (Skill II) 35 min

    PPE means personal protective equipment: a gown, a mask, goggles and gloves. PPE protects you and your patients from germs. Putting it on and taking it off in the right order is Skill II, and you have 6 minutes.

Unit 2 · Beds and comfort

Skills III and IV: unoccupied and occupied beds.

  1. Making an unoccupied bed (Skill III) 30 min

    A clean, smooth bed helps patients rest and keeps their skin healthy. An unoccupied bed is one with no one in it. Skill III has 24 steps and 10 minutes. The secret is working on one side until it is done.

  2. Making an occupied bed (Skill IV) 30 min

    Sometimes a patient cannot get out of bed. You can still give them clean sheets by rolling the patient from side to side. Skill IV has 37 steps and 12 minutes. Keeping the patient safe, covered and comfortable is the…

Unit 3 · Admission and safe moving

Skills V and VI: admitting a patient and bed-to-wheelchair transfer.

  1. Admitting a patient (Skill V) 35 min

    Coming into a hospital or nursing home can feel scary. The admitting caregiver is often the first friendly face a patient meets. Skill V has 16 steps and 10 minutes. You will put on an ID bracelet, check belongings and…

  2. Transferring a patient with a weak side (Skill VI) 35 min

    Moving a patient from bed to a wheelchair is one of the most common caregiver tasks—and one of the riskiest. A fall can cause broken bones. Skill VI has 20 steps and 6 minutes. A gait belt, good body mechanics and the…

Unit 4 · Vital signs and ostomy care

Skill VII (worth the most points) and Skill VIII.

  1. Temperature, pulse and respirations (Skill VII, part 1) 35 min

    Vital signs are the body’s “signs of life.” They tell the nurse how a patient is doing. Skill VII is the biggest skill in Personal Care: 12 minutes for temperature, pulse, respirations and blood pressure. This lesson…

  2. Measuring blood pressure with an aneroid cuff (Skill VII, part 2) 35 min

    Blood pressure is the push of blood against the walls of the arteries. To measure it, you squeeze the arm with a cuff and listen with a stethoscope. This lesson finishes Skill VII. Your readings must be within 2 mm Hg…

  3. Ostomy care (Skill VIII) 35 min
